title: RTD Alerts Residents to Possible Downtown Denver Transit Disruptions Due to Potential Demonstrations - NewsBreak
text:
18 minutes ago The Regional Transportation District (RTD) is preparing for possible demonstrations in downtown Denver today, November 5, 2025. The agency has announced plans to respond if protests disrupt bus and rail services. RTD has identified 21 bus routes that may be affected. These include routes 0, 6, 10, 15, 15L, 8, 9, 32, 19, 48, 16, 52, ART, 0L, 1, 3L, 44, 83L, 83D, EV, and CV.
RTD staff are working with the Denver Police Department and other partners to ensure public safety and reduce service disruptions. The RTD Transit Police Department will increase patrols in the downtown area. RTD will monitor the situation and adjust services as needed based on updates from public safety officials.
Customers are advised to plan ahead for travel to and from downtown Denver. RTD recommends using the Next Ride app and checking Service Alerts for real-time updates. The trip planner tool can help riders find other transit options if needed.
Light rail and commuter rail services to Denver Union Station will continue as scheduled if it is safe. If Union Station closes for safety reasons, connections will be suspended, but trains will continue on the rest of their lines. Light rail service into the Downtown Loop remains suspended due to the Downtown Rail Reconstruction Project.
RTD asks riders to be patient, expect large crowds, and stay informed by signing up for Service Alerts or checking the RTD website. Customers can report safety or security issues using the RTD Transit Watch app. Customer care agents are available daily at 303.299.6000 for questions or concerns.
